# Chapter One — The Brass Key

Mara, whom Ivo alone calls Mar, promises to return the brass key before the winter tide. A red paper boat waits under the harbor lamp.

The narrator insists this happened on Tuesday, then admits that his calendar was blank.

# Chapter Two — The Folded Lighthouse

Mara dreams that the lighthouse folds into a suitcase. When she wakes, the key is still beneath her pillow and the lighthouse stands across the bay.

Old Oren delivers one warning about the northern road and leaves on the noon ferry.

# Chapter Three — Before the Promise

Three years earlier, Ivo found the same red paper boat beside the locked archive. The archive fire followed because he used the brass key.

Ivo calls another woman Mar across the platform, but the narrator cannot see her face.

# Chapter Eighteen — Winter Tide

Mara returns the brass key, preventing Ivo from opening the flooded archive again. The red paper boat passes beneath the harbor lamp and sails out to sea.

The narrator concedes that the first meeting happened on Wednesday, not Tuesday.

# Coda — Clear Water

At dawn the ferry crosses the quiet bay. No promise remains unpaid, and nobody speaks.
